title: TravelPlanner: A Benchmark for Real-World Planning with Language Agents

paper.authors: Xie, Zhang, Chen, Zhu, Lou, Tian, Xiao, Su
paper.venue: ICML 2024 (arXiv v4 2024-10-23 used for this card)
paper.repo_note: Scaffold only found a glued AutoGPT citation link; the paper's own repo is OSU-NLP-Group/TravelPlanner (cloned here). HEAD (2024-10+) contains post-paper additions (ollama backend, gradio, fine-tuning data); pin to this commit and diff agents/ + evaluation/ against the Feb-2024 history before running.

dependence.note: The evaluated object is the LLM-powered agent (ReAct tool use + planning) and every number in Table 3 is a property of the backbone model. Secondary 'component' dependence: natural-language plans are converted to JSON by a GPT-4-Turbo extraction call (Sec. 3.4 fn.1, App. B.3.5, postprocess/parsing.py hard-codes gpt-4-1106-preview) before the rule-based evaluator runs.

claim.statement: In the two-stage mode (ReAct information collection with 6 tools + planning), the GPT-4-Turbo agent delivers a plan for ~90% of queries but reaches a Final Pass Rate of only 0.6% (validation #180: delivery 89.4, commonsense micro/macro 61.1/2.8, hard-constraint micro/macro 15.2/10.6, final 0.6; test #1,000: 93.1/63.3/2.0/10.5/5.5/0.6), i.e. current language agents cannot handle multi-constraint planning (Table 3; Sec. 4.2).
claim.metric: Final Pass Rate = share of delivered plans satisfying all commonsense (8) and hard constraints; plus Delivery Rate, Commonsense/Hard Constraint micro & macro pass rates (Eq. 1-2), computed by evaluation/eval.py on JSON-parsed plans
claim.original_source: Table 3 (main results), Table 4 (per-constraint pass rates, test set), Figure 2 (error distribution); no per-query result files are released in the repo

protocol.model: gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 (PROXY). The paper only says 'GPT-4-Turbo (OpenAI, 2023)'; the repo's supported-model list and postprocess default are gpt-4-1106-preview, which is dead (shutdown 2026-03-26). gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 is the nearest still-callable snapshot of the same product line, not the snapshot used.
protocol.model_status: gpt-4-1106-preview: dead (2026-03-26). gpt-4-turbo / gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09: dying, shutdown 2026-10-23 (target_models.json)
protocol.endpoint: POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions via langchain_community ChatOpenAI (openai==0.27.2, langchain==0.1.4 pinned in requirements.txt)
protocol.prompt_source: agents/prompts.py (ZEROSHOT_REACT_INSTRUCTION for tool use; PLANNER_INSTRUCTION for the planner); postprocess/openai_request.py build_plan_format_conversion_prompt (extraction) = App. B.3.1, B.3.2, B.3.5 verbatim
pipeline: 1. ReAct agent (agents/tool_agents.py ReactAgent): per step two LLM calls (Thought, Action); tools = FlightSearch, GoogleDistanceMatrix, AccommodationSearch, RestaurantSearch, AttractionSearch, CitySearch, NotebookWrite, Planner; max_steps=30, max_retries=3 (early stop after 3 consecutive failed/identical actions); previous observation masked in scratchpad once a new search succeeds
2. Planner call (tools/planner/apis.py Planner.run): PLANNER_INSTRUCTION + notebook contents + query; returns 'Max Token Length Exceeded.' if prompt > 12,000 tokens (tiktoken gpt-3.5-turbo encoding)
3. Post-processing (postprocess/parsing.py -> element_extraction.py -> combination.py): LLM extraction of plan into JSON (temperature 0), then evaluation/eval.py

extraction_llm.model: gpt-4-1106-preview in code (use the same live proxy model in the re-run)

params.seed: not reported / not set; single run per configuration in the paper

protocol.n_items: validation 180 (20 per level x days group) + test 1,000; train 45 not used for evaluation
protocol.samples_per_item: 1 in the paper (temperature 0). Re-run: 3 repeated runs (ANALYSIS_PLAN Sec. 3) x 2 prompt paraphrases limited to the instruction preamble (tool syntax must stay verbatim, otherwise parse_action breaks)
protocol.evaluation: Automatic, rule-based (evaluation/commonsense_constraint.py, hard_constraint.py, eval.py) against the static sandbox database and per-query hard constraints from the HF dataset; OFFLINE evaluation is only possible for train/validation (eval.py supports set_type train|validation). Test-set labels are not released ('level, days, query' only) -> test scores require submission to the HF leaderboard space osunlp/TravelPlannerLeaderboard.
protocol.execution_environment: Python 3.9 conda env from requirements.txt (langchain==0.1.4, openai==0.27.2, tiktoken==0.4.0, datasets, pandas, func_timeout). Sandbox database (CSV files for ~4M records: flights 3.8M rows, restaurants, attractions, accommodations, distance matrix, cities) must be downloaded from the Google Drive link in README and unzipped into the repo root; tools are local pandas lookups (no external API, no docker, no network beyond OpenAI). HF dataset osunlp/TravelPlanner (validation/test queries). Each query runs 20-60 sequential LLM calls; a 180-query validation run is ~2-4 h wall-clock single-threaded.
protocol.representative_subset: Validation split (180 queries, all 9 level x days groups, 20 each) x 2 repeated runs, two-stage mode, GPT-4-Turbo proxy. This is exactly the offline-evaluable half of the original claim (validation final pass rate 0.6% = 1/180). Optional add-on: sole-planning Direct on the same 180 (1 planner call per query, ~$0.10/query) for the 4.4% secondary number.
protocol.environment_check: Before any LLM call: run evaluation/eval.py on the 180 human-annotated validation reference plans (database/validation_ref_info.jsonl + HF 'annotated_plan') and confirm 100% final pass rate, to separate evaluator/database drift from model drift.

artifacts.data_path: HF osunlp/TravelPlanner (train/validation/test queries; validation has reference_information + annotated_plan); database/ (validation_ref_info.jsonl etc.); sandbox DB via Google Drive link in README (not in git)
artifacts.eval_path: evaluation/eval.py, evaluation/commonsense_constraint.py, evaluation/hard_constraint.py; postprocess/parsing.py, element_extraction.py, combination.py, format_check.py
artifacts.data_license: HF dataset: cc-by-4.0; code: MIT; sandbox DB: no explicit license (derived/modified from Kaggle Airbnb & Zomato dumps and Google Maps API outputs per App. A.3)
artifacts.notes: Test-set ground truth withheld (leaderboard only). No original per-query agent trajectories or model outputs are released, so no paired per-item comparison is possible; only aggregate Table 3 numbers. README forbids benchmark-specific prompt engineering (Warnings) - paraphrase variants must stay generic.

blockers: Exact original snapshot (gpt-4-1106-preview) is dead; live arm is a same-line proxy (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09)
Test-set (1,000) evaluation requires leaderboard submission; only validation (180) is evaluable offline
LLM-dependent post-processing step (plan-to-JSON extraction) is itself part of the protocol and must use a live model
Cost: ~$1.45 per two-stage query at gpt-4-turbo pricing (20-60 calls per query)
Sandbox database is hosted on Google Drive (not versioned); must be hashed and archived at run time

baseline_alive.purpose: proxy live baseline for the paper's 'GPT-4-Turbo' (original snapshot gpt-4-1106-preview is dead)

gemini (current dated snapshot at run time)
llama (open weights, e.g. Llama-3.x/4 instruct, weight hash pinned)

budget.unit_basis: Per two-stage query: ~32 ReAct calls (thought+action) x ~3.8K input / ~60 output tokens (instruction ~1.6K + scratchpad with one unmasked tool observation), + 1 planner call (~8K in / ~1.5K out), + 1 extraction call (~2.5K in / ~0.8K out) = ~34 calls, ~132K in, ~4.2K out, ~$1.45. No cost statement in the paper; estimate from code structure and Table 5 tool-use counts.

full.definition: validation 180 + test 1,000 queries, two-stage mode, 3 repeated runs (test scoring via leaderboard)

subset.definition: validation 180 x 2 repeated runs (offline-evaluable; preserves the 0.6% validation claim)

budget.cap_usd: to be set by user (recommend 600 for the subset incl. retries)

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN Sec. 1, capability_limit. Reference number: validation Final Pass Rate 0.6% (1/180; Clopper-Pearson 95% CI 0.01-3.1%). SURVIVED if the median (over runs x paraphrases) re-run final pass rate lies within 0-3.1% AND hard-constraint macro pass rate stays < 20% (same order of magnitude as 10.6) AND direction 'agents cannot handle the task' holds. PARTIAL if final pass rate is 3.1-10% (outside CI but still an order of magnitude below a usable level) or delivery/commonsense numbers move by > 15 points while final pass rate stays < 10%. DEAD if final pass rate >= 10% (i.e. >= 18/180) or the claim 'no LLM other than GPT-4 solves any task' is not the relevant framing anymore because the proxy model solves a substantial share.
judgment.notes: Temperature 0 -> run-to-run variance comes from API nondeterminism and early-stop rules; report per-run values and bootstrap CI over 180 queries. Because the live arm is a snapshot proxy, any judgment must be labelled 'proxy-arm' in the analysis (sensitivity scenario ANALYSIS_PLAN Sec. 2 item 2). Paraphrase variants must not alter tool syntax or constraint descriptions (README Warnings).

domain_notes: The environment is a closed, static sandbox (all six tools are local CSV lookups), so environment drift is nil once the Google-Drive database is archived with a hash; the human-annotated validation plans give a free evaluator sanity check (must score 100%). The protocol has two LLM-dependent stages (agent + JSON extraction) and an aggressive early-stop policy (3 identical/failed actions), so delivery rate is as informative as the final pass rate. Expect the successor arms to change the picture qualitatively (later leaderboard entries report >>0.6%), which is precisely the capability_limit survival question.
